executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, 2026) and PAHO (October 2025–May 2026) reveals multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the highest-priority select agent concern, with ongoing animal-sector detections and continued pandemic spillover risk warranting BSL-3 handling protocols. Mpox, Yellow Fever, and Dengue are generating sustained epidemiological alerts across the Americas, while the Southern Hemisphere's influenza season onset compounds respiratory burden. Pertussis resurges regionally and measles transmission persists in the Americas, signaling vaccine-preventable disease pressure alongside vector-borne and zoonotic threats.
bottomLine: Concurrent H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk, escalating vector-borne disease burden in the Americas, and resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases constitute the dominant global health security concerns for mid-2026.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained animal-sector circulation
Ongoing risk of zoonotic spillover to humans with case fatality rates historically exceeding 50%
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential; ECDC concurrent monitoring through Week 20 2026
Mammalian host detections expanding potential bridging populations to humans
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce BSL-3 protocols for all specimen handling; pre-position antiviral stockpiles; coordinate with FAO/OIE on poultry sector containment and accelerate H5N1 human vaccine readiness assessments

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active transmission
Concurrent ECDC monitoring in weekly threat reports Weeks 16-20 2026 suggesting cross-regional concern
BSL-3 select agent classification requiring enhanced containment and contact tracing
Potential clade diversification risk given ongoing African clade I emergence context
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing networks across the Americas; ensure ring vaccination availability with JYNNEOS/MVA-BN; enforce BSL-3 laboratory protocols; coordinate with CDC and ECDC on genomic sequencing to monitor clade evolution

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Epizootic activity in non-human primates typically precedes human spillover events
BSL-3 pathogen with case fatality rates of 20-50% in severe cases
Vaccination coverage gaps in endemic zones increase outbreak amplification risk
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; intensify entomological and epizootics surveillance in sylvatic zones; maintain emergency vaccine stockpiles through PAHO/PAHO EPI; issue travel health advisories for affected corridors

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update 18 February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Historically record dengue transmission in the Americas in 2024-2025 creating sensitized populations and serotype shifts
Co-circulation of multiple serotypes increases severe dengue risk
Climate-driven expansion of Aedes aegypti vector habitat extending transmission season
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations including larval source reduction; strengthen hospital surge capacity for severe dengue management; promote integrated vector management; monitor serotype circulation for secondary infection risk populations

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Onset)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert 27 April 2026 marking official start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Concurrent circulation with RSV noted since January 2026 alert, straining respiratory care capacity
Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season transition data available for strain forecasting
Potential H5N1 co-infection risk with seasonal strains complicating clinical differentiation
threats.action: Ensure Southern Hemisphere vaccine formulation distribution is complete; reinforce sentinel surveillance networks; prepare healthcare systems for dual influenza-RSV surge; maintain oseltamivir stockpiles and promote infection control measures in healthcare settings

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Dual PAHO updates in December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Cyclic epidemic patterns amplified by waning immunity in adolescents and adults
Neonatal mortality risk in under-vaccinated communities
Possible contribution of emerging macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis strains
threats.action: Audit Tdap booster coverage in adolescents, adults, and pregnant women; strengthen birth dose and infant immunization schedules; investigate antibiotic resistance patterns in circulating strains; enhance surveillance in neonatal and pediatric settings

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert 3 February 2026 indicating active transmission in the Americas
Measles elimination status at risk due to vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic
ECDC concurrent monitoring in weekly reports suggests imported case pressure in Europe
Highly contagious pathogen with R0 of 12-18 enabling rapid outbreak amplification in under-immunized clusters
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments and catch-up campaigns targeting susceptible cohorts; investigate importation chains; enforce outbreak response immunization within 72 hours of case confirmation; strengthen genomic sequencing for genotype tracking

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika in shared Aedes vector populations complicates differential diagnosis
Potential for new geographic expansion as Aedes albopictus range extends
Chronic arthralgia burden in affected populations with significant long-term morbidity
threats.action: Enhance syndromic surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue clinically; strengthen laboratory diagnostic capacity for arboviral co-infections; coordinate vector control with dengue programs; alert clinicians to long-term rheumatological sequelae management

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are identified in current surveillance: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (Critical) with sustained animal-sector circulation and documented zoonotic spillover potential in the Americas per PAHO updates from November 2025 and March 2026, and Monkeypox virus/Mpox (Elevated) with active human transmission across the Americas per PAHO April 2026 update. Yellow Fever virus (BSL-3) also merits flag given active PAHO alert from March 2026. All three require BSL-3 containment protocols for specimen handling, with H5N1 representing the highest pandemic risk among these select agents.
amrSignals: Potential macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis contributing to pertussis resurgence across the Americas given dual PAHO alerts within 3 months
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) may indicate counterfeit pharmaceutical circulation potentially compounded by antimicrobial misuse in same supply chains
Methanol poisoning alert (PAHO October 2025) suggests illicit substance market activity that may co-occur with antibiotic misuse and substandard medicine distribution networks
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden: H5N1 zoonotic pressure, seasonal influenza Southern Hemisphere onset, RSV co-circulation, and pertussis resurgence create compounding respiratory healthcare demand across the Americas in Q2 2026
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence: Dual measles and pertussis alerts within weeks of each other indicate post-pandemic immunization gap consequences now manifesting in outbreak dynamics

Arboviral disease convergence: Concurrent dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever alerts in overlapping geographic zones suggest shared ecological drivers including climate-linked vector expansion and urbanization

BSL-3 select agent co-occurrence: Simultaneous H5N1 animal sector activity and mpox human transmission creates dual high-containment pathogen monitoring burden on public health laboratory infrastructure

Non-communicable disease mimicry risk: GLP-1 medication misuse and methanol poisoning alerts indicate toxic exposure events that may present to surveillance systems as infectious disease clusters, requiring differential diagnosis protocols
ECDC five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, 2026) suggest sustained multi-hazard surveillance posture in Europe with imported disease pressure from the Americas and Africa
